clue.text: One, say, about to pull in line on river

definitions.text: One, say, about to pull in

parts.note: a line is an approach or point of view, as is an angle
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A fisherman on the riverbank is about to reel in his line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. 'Line' seems to belong to the fishing picture, but it means a take or slant on something.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman with a bite is someone about to haul in a catch, so the cryptic definition describes one example.

clue.text: Chum possibly made from two portions of ground meat

indicators.note: ground meat is minced up, so the letters are broken down and remade

parts.note: the first of two portions of the word that follows
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some pet food is made from minced meat, as tinned dog chum might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chum' suggests the dog food brand, but it is a friend; the meat is used twice before being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow member of one's side is one kind of pal, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Overweight cops left for dead

indicators.note: to cop is to catch or grab, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: overweight means fat
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Police officers who are overweight have been left for dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cops' reads as police, but it is a verb meaning catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery or a market without life is described as either word, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: I'll settle to get rid of credit limits

indicators.note: the abbreviation forms the boundaries, sitting at either end of the other piece

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit
to get rid of something is to lose it

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to pay off a debt to escape their credit limit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person: the answer is the one who says 'I'll settle' it, as a pitcher or deal-maker finishes things off.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who finishes a game or clinches a sale is the one who brings matters to a conclusion.

clue.text: Organ grinder's heart eaten by bear

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater

parts.note: to lug is to carry or bear a load

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the centre letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: An organ grinder's monkey gets eaten by a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ grinder' looks like one phrase, but 'Organ' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The breathing organ in the chest is a body organ, so this is an example.

clue.text: Raft I'd lost at sea

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A castaway laments the raft they have lost at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean floating without control or direction, and figuratively bewildered.

clue.text: High jumper rocks during walk

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits inside it

parts.note: to trog is British slang for walking wearily
a reef is a ridge of rocks near the sea surface

explanation.surface: A high jumper's performance rocks while athletes are walking about.
explanation.walkthrough: TROG is informal British for trudge along.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphibian that climbs trees and leaps between branches is a jumper found high up.

clue.text: Knight led astray, taking drugs in sewer

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: going astray means wandering from the right path, so the letters move out of order

parts.note: taken as written
E is ecstasy, so two of them are drugs, taken in with the other letters

explanation.surface: A knight is led astray and takes drugs down in the sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain, but it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tool that pulls thread through cloth is the thing that does the stitching.

clue.text: Around fifty, one begins to struggle

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a founder is one who starts something up
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Around the age of fifty, a person starts to find life a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To flail or blunder about helplessly is to struggle, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: After losing the lead, it's pointless

definitions.text: After losing the lead, it's pointless

parts.words: After losing the lead, it's pointless
parts.note: surface reading: a team that has lost its lead in a match has nothing to play for
setter's reading: a writing tool without its graphite core cannot have a sharp tip

explanation.surface: A competitor who has lost their lead feels there is no point in carrying on.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead here is graphite, and pointless means literally lacking a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden writing stick whose graphite has gone can never be sharpened to a tip.

clue.text: Vast lake on isle obscured with mist

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: something obscured is blurred and confused, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge lake beside an island is hidden in fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without bounds is enormous, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Cover of Kids on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so sound counts and not spelling

parts.note: to guy someone is to tease or make fun of them

explanation.surface: A cover version of a song by a band called Kids is played on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kids' looks like children, but it is a verb meaning teases; 'guy' is that verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A false outward appearance is a front or disguise, a cover for what lies behind.

clue.text: Propose kicking bishop's butt

indicators.note: kicking out means expelling, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to broach a subject is to raise or propose it
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone suggests giving a bishop a kick up the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after bishop is the link 'has', not a possessive. A roach is the stub of a cannabis joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The leftover end of a smoked joint is slang for a cigarette end.

clue.text: Withdraw £10 from Halifax for port

indicators.note: withdrawing money takes it out, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
the pound sign is L, from libra, and ten is X in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A customer takes out ten pounds from the Halifax, a British bank, to buy a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: The Halifax is a British bank, so the surface is about a cash withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Israeli city on the Mediterranean is a major seaport.

clue.text: Worker in wood seeing grouse on log

parts.note: to carp is to complain or grouse
to log something is to record or enter it

explanation.surface: A woodcutter spots a grouse perched on a log.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' and 'log' both look like nouns from the woods; both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who builds things in timber is a craftsman in that material.

clue.text: English and American soldiers rejected evacuation

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so these letters run the other way

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: British and American troops turned down an evacuation plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the American soldiers are turned round; English stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema clears the bowels, and evacuation is the medical word for emptying them.

clue.text: Dish of the day: southern fried plaice

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern

indicators.note: frying cooks and transforms food, so the letters are changed in form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A restaurant board announces today's dish: fried plaice cooked the southern way.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's featured dish not on the regular menu is called today's offering.

clue.text: Ultimate sign of diabetes: urine sample containing most sugar

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
wee is informal for urine
to sample something is to test it

explanation.surface: The final proof of diabetes is a urine sample with very high sugar levels.
explanation.walkthrough: WEE is informal British for urine.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of sugary describes whatever has the highest sugar content.

clue.text: Work space at home has grand entrance

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
an en is a printer's space
someone at home is in
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A home office has an impressive front door.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is the printer's space half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap or aperture through which one comes in is a way in.

clue.text: I also picked up a pair of socks

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: also means too

explanation.surface: Someone collected a couple of socks from the floor too.
explanation.walkthrough: A sock is a punch, so a pair of them is the boxer's quick left-right combination.
explanation.definitionFit: Two punches thrown in quick succession make the boxing combination named after counting.

clue.text: Some paint on a coat such as this

definitions.text: Some paint on a coat such as this

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters lie within the phrase

parts.note: found running through these words

explanation.surface: A fresco painter applies paint onto a layer of plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: in fresco, paint is applied to this final wet plaster layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine final coat of plaster on which a fresco is painted is the surface that receives the pigment.

clue.text: A group of Mounties plan a demanding walk

indicators.note: a group of letters is taken as a run from within the words that follow

parts.note: found running through these words

explanation.surface: Canadian police officers organise a gruelling hike.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade along a seafront is a level public path for strolling.

clue.text: Ape that flies

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mimic or copy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like a noun, a primate that cannot fly; it is the verb to imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means repeat mechanically, and the noun is a bright tropical bird that copies speech.

clue.text: Soldier perhaps, firing missiles primarily?

parts.note: surface reading: an artillery or rocket soldier whose main job is launching missiles
setter's reading: the missiles are arrows, shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A soldier's main task might be launching rockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missiles' suggests modern weapons, but arrows are missiles too, and a bowman's main job is shooting them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman in an old army was a soldier whose role was shooting arrows at the enemy.

clue.text: Old person regularly sampling jazz at beach

indicators.note: sampling at regular intervals takes every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: An elderly person dips into some jazz down at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old person' wants to be an elderly listener; it means a member of an ancient people.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Mexican civilisation conquered by Spain is a person from an ancient culture.

clue.text: Professor's lectures likely to offend

indicators.note: lectures are spoken out, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: a professor teaches a course

explanation.surface: A professor's lectures are probably offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lectures' looks like the thing being judged, but it signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude or vulgar language is apt to give offence.

clue.text: Corporation taking on human resources drone

indicators.note: taking on staff brings them inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a tum
HR is the abbreviation for human resources

explanation.surface: A large company hires an HR department full of dull workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation in old slang means a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A low continuous humming sound is a drone.

clue.text: Male with head shaved on top?

definitions.text: Male with head shaved on top?

indicators.note: shaving the top off removes the uppermost letter, which in a down answer is the first

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
conk is British slang for the head or nose

explanation.surface: A man has shaved the top of his head.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a religious man with a tonsure, shaved on the crown. Conk is old British slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Men in some religious orders traditionally wore a tonsure, a shaved patch on the crown.

clue.text: Frighten a seal with a joyful outburst

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate
taken as written
a bung is a stopper that seals a hole
'with' joins on another letter taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone startles a seal and shouts with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' suggests the animal, but it is a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfers' cry of exhilaration, popularised by cartoon turtles, is a gleeful exclamation.

clue.text: A bit that gets cast?

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould anew, so the letters are thrown into new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small piece is thrown out on a fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a morsel cast into the water to lure fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel of food thrown on a hook to attract fish is the lure.

clue.text: Pampered politician ultimately blocks satirical piece by editor

indicators.note: something that blocks sits in the way, inside the other piece

parts.note: a spoof is a parody

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A cosseted MP tries to suppress a satirical sketch by a newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given everything without effort, as a baby is fed, is to be indulged or spoilt.

clue.text: Self-righteous at church surrounded by saints and stars

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, sanctimonious

indicators.note: surrounded means enclosed on all sides, so these go inside

parts.note: S is short for saint, so two of them
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Sanctimonious worshippers at church are surrounded by saints and celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' simply puts the pious piece first; only the church goes inside the two saints.
explanation.definitionFit: This zodiac sign is a constellation, a group of stars.
